title: Chand Baori, Abhaneri
summary: Chand Baori is a stepwell at Abhaneri in Dausa district, Rajasthan, built in the 8th-9th century; Lonely Planet credits the Hindu king Raja Chanda. Rajasthan Tourism gives it as 19.5 m deep with 13 storeys, and Lonely Planet as about 35 m across, with some 3,500 steps arranged in a criss-cross pattern down the sides of the central tank.

uncertainty.note: Incredible India (Dausa page) gives the 8th-9th century; Rajasthan Tourism says the eighth century and Lonely Planet the ninth, so the range is 700-900 CE. End is the present: the well stands.

reviewer_note: Shape block (stepwell, per instructions): the height is depth below ground and the plan is the side. The 35 m side is from Lonely Planet only; I did not find a heritage-body or scholarly page giving a plan dimension (ASI page unreachable), so the plan is less sure than the 19.5 m depth. Depth conflicts: 19.5 m (Rajasthan Tourism, a published paper repeating it) vs about 98 feet (Incredible India Jaipur page). Step count also conflicts: 1,000 (Rajasthan Tourism) vs 3,500 (Incredible India, Lonely Planet), so no step count is used. Date range wide on purpose.
